clue.text: Bribes generated amidst suspicious behaviour

indicators.note: amidst places one word in the middle of another, flanked on both sides

parts.note: sus is informal British slang for suspicious, as in the old 'sus laws'
something generated has been brought into being

explanation.surface: Someone acting shiftily turns out to be handing over bribes.
explanation.walkthrough: SUS is British slang for suspect or suspicious, as in the old 'sus laws' on stop and search.
explanation.definitionFit: To suborn is to induce someone, typically by payment, into wrongdoing such as perjury.

clue.text: Winter transport requiring a lot of dexterity

indicators.note: a lot of something is not quite all of it, so the final letter goes

parts.note: sleight, as in sleight of hand, means nimble skill

explanation.surface: Steering a vehicle through the snow takes real skill.
explanation.walkthrough: SLEIGHT loses its last letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleigh is a sledge drawn by horses or reindeer over snow and ice.

clue.text: Rudimentary matters around American measures of speed

indicators.note: around has the first item wrapped about the second, enclosing it

parts.note: buds are the undeveloped beginnings of flowers or leaves
A is a standard abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: Basic issues surround American rates of speed.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes inside BUDS, after the B.
explanation.definitionFit: A baud is a unit of signalling rate in data transmission, one symbol per second.

clue.text: Regret impounding European spaceship for subsequent release

indicators.note: impounding means shutting something away inside an enclosure

parts.note: to rue is to regret
E is the abbreviation for European
the International Space Station, a crewed orbital craft

explanation.surface: Someone regrets confiscating a European spacecraft that was later let go.
explanation.walkthrough: The ISS is the International Space Station, a common crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A reissue is a further release of a book, record or stamp after the original one.

clue.text: Excessive pace requiring extra energy

indicators.note: requiring extra suggests something added into the word to make it complete

parts.note: a pace is a single step
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Keeping up a punishing speed needs more stamina.
explanation.walkthrough: E slips into STEP, beside the existing E.
explanation.definitionFit: A steep price or demand is unreasonably high, an informal sense meaning too much.

clue.text: Shakespearean figure backed genuine revolution in scenery etc

indicators.note: backed means going backwards, so the word is read from its end

parts.note: genuine means real

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so this word is also read the other way

parts.note: a stage set is the scenery and props

explanation.surface: A theatrical character spins round on stage among the scenery.
explanation.walkthrough: REAL backwards gives LAER and SET backwards gives TES.
explanation.definitionFit: Laertes is the brother of Ophelia in Hamlet, who kills the prince in the final duel.

clue.text: Produced farmyard noises, incorporating common vulgarity ultimately — this?

definitions.text: Produced farmyard noises, incorporating common vulgarity ultimately — this?

indicators.note: incorporating takes something into the body of another word

parts.note: cattle low, so mooing cows lowed
com is a standard abbreviation for common

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very last letter of the word it follows

parts.note: the final letter of vulgarity

explanation.surface: Mooing noises and a bit of vulgarity: the clue asks whether that is a style of humour.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue, farmyard noises plus crudeness, also describes the answer, which is what 'this?' prompts.
explanation.definitionFit: Low comedy is broad humour relying on slapstick, crude jokes and farce rather than wit.

clue.text: Say good leader of teachers should be intellectual

parts.note: e.g. means for example, as does say
G is the abbreviation for good
a head teacher leads a school's staff

explanation.surface: A school's head ought to be a clever person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' gives EG, the abbreviation for 'for example'.
explanation.definitionFit: An egghead is an informal, slightly mocking word for a highly academic, bookish person.

clue.text: Sudden attacks securing Australian policy change

indicators.note: securing means holding something firmly within, enclosing it

parts.note: two words for an attack of illness: a turn and a bout
A is a standard abbreviation for Australian

explanation.surface: Abrupt assaults capture an Australian, forcing a change of plan.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'attacks' asks for two separate words, with the abbreviation held between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnabout is a complete reversal of position, opinion or policy, also called a U-turn.

clue.text: Police officer not losing heart after quantity of work in the main

indicators.note: after puts one part later in the word than the other
in places one word inside another

parts.note: the main is a poetic term for the open sea
the erg is a unit of work or energy

indicators.note: losing its heart means the middle letter goes, keeping only the outside

parts.note: the first and last letters of not

explanation.surface: An officer keeps up their spirits after a stint of work at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is an old poetic name for the ocean; the erg is the small CGS unit of work.
explanation.definitionFit: A sergeant is a police rank above constable and below inspector in Britain.

clue.text: Displaying knowledge? English not polite about it

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English

indicators.note: about means surrounding, placed around another part

parts.note: rude is the opposite of polite
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Englishman shows off what he knows and is rude about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is loose: being learned is shown by displaying knowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: Erudite describes someone showing great learning and scholarship, a fitting description.

clue.text: German composer replaces note with a show of hesitation, I bet

definitions.note: a cryptic definition: the person who says 'I bet' is one

indicators.note: replaces swaps one element in a word for something else

parts.note: Richard Wagner, composer of the Ring cycle
N stands for note
er is the sound people make when hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone bets that Wagner would have hesitated over a note.
explanation.walkthrough: In WAGNER the N is replaced by ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone who says 'I bet' is placing a wager, which makes the speaker a gambler of that kind.

clue.text: Government obscurations concealing initial main points

indicators.note: concealing the initial hides the first letter from view

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for government
mists obscure the view

explanation.surface: A government fog hides the key facts of an issue.
explanation.walkthrough: MISTS loses its M. 'Main' looks attached to 'initial' but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The gist of something is its essential substance or central thrust, so gists are its key ideas.

clue.text: Drop name outrageously before end of some walk

indicators.note: before puts the jumbled part ahead of the next piece
doing something outrageously means wildly, so these letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: taken as written for the jumble

indicators.note: end of takes only the final letter of the following word

parts.note: the last letter of some

explanation.surface: A name-dropper shamelessly boasts during a stroll.
explanation.definitionFit: A promenade is a leisurely stroll, or the paved seafront path where people take one.

clue.text: Parasites understand about new publican

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the pair goes round the next piece

parts.note: lice are parasitic insects
'I see' means I understand
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: The new landlord grasps the problem of bugs in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' here means the two words together wrap the single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a publican holds the licence to sell alcohol on the premises, making him the licensee.

clue.text: Bird is caught by international physician

indicators.note: something caught by another is trapped inside it

parts.note: int is the abbreviation for international
a tern is a seabird
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bird is caught by a doctor of international standing.
explanation.walkthrough: Internist is mainly an American word for a specialist in internal medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: An internist is a specialist in internal medicine, the American term for a general physician.

clue.text: Mess Rebus sorted out is overwhelming

indicators.note: sorted out means put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written for the jumble; Rebus is Ian Rankin's detective

explanation.surface: Clearing up the detective Rebus's mess is too much to cope with.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspector Rebus is the Edinburgh detective of Ian Rankin's novels.
explanation.definitionFit: To submerse is to plunge under water, figuratively to swamp or overpower, matching third-person 'is overwhelming'.

clue.text: Low period interrupted by river in flood

indicators.note: a word interrupted by something has that thing break into its middle

parts.note: a down is a spell of low spirits, as in ups and downs
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A dry spell is broken by a river bursting its banks.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes into DOWN after the D.
explanation.definitionFit: To drown land is to flood or submerge it completely under water.

clue.text: No performance in church for romantic piece

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in places one word inside another

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a turn is a stage act

explanation.surface: A church refuses to stage a love song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Romantic' means of the Romantic era in music, not amorous.
explanation.definitionFit: A nocturne is a dreamy, lyrical composition associated with the Romantic era, notably Chopin's piano works.

clue.text: Settled opinion piece about Tesla

indicators.note: about means surrounding, placed around another part

parts.note: an op-ed is a newspaper opinion column
T is the symbol for the tesla, the unit of magnetic flux density

explanation.surface: A columnist made up their mind in a newspaper piece about the carmaker Tesla.
explanation.walkthrough: T goes inside OPED.
explanation.definitionFit: Having opted, one has chosen or decided, as in settled on a choice.

clue.text: Pathetic person curtailed streak where moviegoers gather

indicators.note: curtailed means having had its tail cut off, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a drip is a feeble, wet person
a vein is a streak, as in a vein of humour or ore

explanation.surface: A feeble character has a brief streak of something where cinema audiences assemble.
explanation.walkthrough: DRIP loses its P.
explanation.definitionFit: A drive-in is an outdoor cinema where audiences watch films from their parked cars.

clue.text: Things that can pierce old fishing gear beside coastal region

indicators.note: beside sets one piece directly next to another

parts.note: a bay is a curved stretch of coast
O is the abbreviation for old
nets are used to catch fish

explanation.surface: Old fishing equipment by the shore is full of sharp hooks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beside' allows either order, and here the coast comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Bayonets are blades fixed to rifles, designed to stab and pierce in close combat.

clue.text: Cloudy, close to covering most of large structure?

indicators.note: covering means wrapping around something and enclosing it

parts.note: near means close to

indicators.note: most of means all but the last letter

parts.note: bulk is great size, a large mass or body

explanation.surface: A vast building looks hazy when you get near it.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'large structure' is a loose description of bulk, great size or mass.
explanation.definitionFit: Nebular relates to a nebula, an interstellar cloud of gas and dust, hence hazy or misty.

clue.text: Large vessels? Possible limitation to arrangement with a small

indicators.note: a possible version is just one of several ways the letters might be arranged

parts.note: a rota is a fixed arrangement of duties that limits who works when
taken as written
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A query about big ships and a scheduling restriction.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the vessels are blood vessels, not ships.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorta is the main artery carrying blood from the heart, the largest blood vessel in the body.

clue.text: Agitate and resist delay

indicators.note: to agitate is to stir up and shake, disturbing the order

parts.note: taken as written for the jumble

explanation.surface: A call to stir up protest and resist being held up.
explanation.definitionFit: Tardiness is lateness or slowness, the state of being behind time.

clue.text: Doctors run from fountains

indicators.note: taking one thing from another removes it

parts.note: fountains throw up sprays of water
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Medics sprint away from the fountains.
explanation.walkthrough: SPRAYS loses R. 'Doctors' looks like medics, but it is a verb meaning neuters.
explanation.definitionFit: To doctor an animal is a euphemism for neutering it, and spaying is neutering a female.

clue.text: Donkey's over being attached to sticky part of plant

indicators.note: being attached to joins one piece directly onto another

parts.note: a burr is a prickly seed head that clings to fur and clothing
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A donkey ends up covered in clinging plant matter.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's means 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Burro is the Spanish word for a small donkey, used in the American southwest as a pack animal.

clue.text: Always upset about end of brave deceased actor

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word reads backwards
about means surrounding, placed around another part

parts.note: ever means always

indicators.note: end of takes only the last letter of the following word

parts.note: the last letter of brave

explanation.surface: An actor known for bravery has died, to everyone's lasting distress.
explanation.walkthrough: EVER reversed is REVE, which goes round E. Christopher Reeve, who played Superman, died in 2004.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Reeve was the American actor famous as Superman, who died in 2004 after a riding accident.

clue.text: Acquisitive financiers I discovered amongst brokers, wasting time

indicators.note: amongst places one item in the midst of another
wasting time throws away the letter that stands for time

parts.note: traders buy and sell on behalf of clients
taken as written

explanation.surface: I find predatory investors among dealers who are idling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discovered' reads as uncovered, but here it only joins: I was found among them.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporate raiders are investors who buy large stakes in companies, aiming at takeover or quick profit.

clue.text: Excellent and fast, suppressing male illness

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, with 1 read as the letter I

indicators.note: suppressing holds something down underneath, keeping it within

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A fit, quick man's sickness is being held down.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, meaning first-rate, is written with the digit read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: An ailment is a minor sickness or complaint, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Adds to writings, erasing beginning but including conclusion

indicators.note: including takes something inside
erasing the beginning rubs out the first letter

parts.note: texts are written works
the end is the conclusion

explanation.surface: A writer revises a manuscript by deleting the opening and adding an ending.
explanation.definitionFit: To extend something is to lengthen or enlarge it, making it bigger by adding more.

clue.text: Hides rocky rubble next to rear parts of garden beds

indicators.note: next to sets one piece directly alongside another

parts.note: scree is loose broken rock on a mountainside

indicators.note: rear parts are the back ends, so the last letters of each word

parts.note: the final letters of garden and beds

explanation.surface: A gardener conceals stony debris behind the flower beds.
explanation.definitionFit: To screen something is to shield or conceal it from view, as with a partition.
